title: Risk Management Concepts

header.html: 1.2 Understand risk management concepts: Risk management lifecycle; Risk management processes
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Risk vocabulary

Term Meaning
Asset Anything of value to the organization: data, systems, people, reputation
Threat A possible cause of harm: an attacker, malware, a flood
Vulnerability A weakness that a threat can use: unpatched software, weak password
Likelihood How probable it is that the threat uses the weakness
Impact The harm if it happens: money, downtime, law, trust
Risk The chance of loss: likelihood combined with impact
Exposure Being open to a threat through a vulnerability

You cannot remove all risk. The goal is to bring risk within what the organization accepts.

Exam tip

. A threat needs a vulnerability to cause risk. A vulnerability with no threat, or a threat with no vulnerability, gives little risk.

2The risk management lifecycle

Risk management is a repeating cycle, not a one-time project.

Step What happens
1 Identify Find the assets, threats and vulnerabilities
2 Assess Estimate likelihood and impact and rank the risks
3 Treat Choose a response for each risk (section 4)
4 Monitor and review Track the risk, test the controls, repeat as things change

Results go into a risk register: a list of risks with an owner, a rating, the treatment and the status. Key risk indicators (KRIs) are measures that warn that risk is rising (Module 6).

3Assessing risk

Method How Result
Qualitative Rate by judgment: low, medium, high; a risk matrix Fast, subjective
Quantitative Use money and numbers Precise, needs data
Quantitative term Meaning
Asset value (AV) What the asset is worth
Exposure factor (EF) The percent of the asset lost in one event
Single loss expectancy (SLE) AV times EF: the loss from one event
Annualized rate of occurrence (ARO) How many times a year the event is expected
Annualized loss expectancy (ALE) SLE times ARO: the expected loss per year

Example: AV of 100,000 dollars and EF of 50 percent give an SLE of 50,000; with an ARO of 0.2 (once in five years) the ALE is 10,000 dollars per year. A safeguard is worth buying when it costs less than the ALE it removes.

Exam tip

. SLE = AV times EF. ALE = SLE times ARO. Do qualitative first when numbers are missing.

4Risk treatment

Response Meaning Example
Avoid Stop the activity that creates the risk Do not store card numbers at all
Mitigate (reduce) Add controls to lower likelihood or impact Patch, encrypt, train staff
Transfer (share) Move the financial impact to someone else Insurance, a contract with a provider
Accept Live with the risk knowingly Low risk, or the control costs more than the loss

Two key limits: risk appetite is how much risk the organization is willing to take to reach its goals; risk tolerance is the acceptable variation around it.

Risk after controls Meaning
Inherent risk The risk before controls
Residual risk The risk that remains after controls; it must be accepted by management
Exam tip

. Insurance transfers the cost, not the responsibility. Residual risk is accepted by management, not by the security team alone.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A server runs unpatched software that a known worm can use. In risk terms, what is the unpatched software?

  • AA vulnerability that a threat can use
  • BA threat that causes loss to the asset
  • CAn asset of value to the business
  • DAn impact on the availability goal
Show the answer

Answer: A. A weakness that a threat can use is a vulnerability; the worm is the threat.

S2A company buys cyber insurance to cover the cost of a breach. Which risk treatment is this?

  • ATransfer of the financial impact
  • BAvoidance of the risky activity
  • CMitigation with technical controls
  • DAcceptance of the full risk
Show the answer

Answer: A. Insurance moves the financial impact to another party, which is risk transfer.

S3A project would store card numbers that the business does not really need. The team decides not to store them. Which treatment is this?

  • AMitigation, because the controls are stronger
  • BTransfer, because the data moves elsewhere
  • CAcceptance, because the risk is low
  • DAvoidance, because the activity is stopped
Show the answer

Answer: D. Stopping the activity that creates the risk is avoidance.

S4An asset is worth 200,000 dollars and a flood would destroy 25 percent of it. What is the single loss expectancy?

  • A25,000 dollars, from the exposure factor alone
  • B200,000 dollars, from the full asset value
  • C50,000 dollars, from asset value times exposure factor
  • D8,000 dollars, from an annual rate of occurrence
Show the answer

Answer: C. SLE equals asset value times exposure factor, 200,000 times 0.25.

S5After controls are applied, some risk remains. Who should formally accept this residual risk?

  • AThe help desk analyst who reported the issue
  • BThe vendor who sold the security product
  • CManagement, who owns the business risk
  • DThe junior security analyst on duty
Show the answer

Answer: C. Residual risk is accepted by management, which owns the business risk.

S6A team rates each risk as low, medium or high on a matrix, without money values. Which assessment method is this?

  • AQuantitative analysis using annual loss figures
  • BA penetration test using attack tools
  • CQualitative analysis using judgment and ratings
  • DA vulnerability scan using a scanner
Show the answer

Answer: C. Ratings and a risk matrix are qualitative assessment.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are the four risk treatment options?

Show the answer

Avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept.

R2What is the formula for annualized loss expectancy?

Show the answer

SLE times ARO.

R3What is residual risk?

Show the answer

The risk that remains after controls.

R4What is a risk register?

Show the answer

A list of risks with owners, ratings, treatments and status.

R5What is risk appetite?

Show the answer

How much risk the organization is willing to take.

R6Does the risk cycle end?

Show the answer

No, it repeats: identify, assess, treat, monitor.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Risk threat uses a vulnerability to harm an asset; likelihood and impact
Lifecycle identify, assess, treat, monitor and review; repeat
Qualitative / quantitative ratings and matrix / money values
Formulas SLE = AV times EF; ALE = SLE times ARO
Treatments avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept
Residual risk what remains; management accepts it
